## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Puṭadūsakajātaka* (Ja 280) is a story in the Jātaka collection, positioned as the tenth tale of the *Araññavagga* [Fausböll 1879]. The text opens with the phrase *Addhā hi nūna migarājā* [Fausböll 1879]. According to its traditional frame story, the Buddha recounted the jātaka while staying at Jetavana, occasioned by a destroyer of leaf-baskets or pottles (*puṭadūsaka*) when a minister in Sāvatthī invited the monastic order headed by the Buddha into a park [Fausböll 1879]. In the story's conclusion (*samodhāna*), the Buddha identifies the Bodhisatta as the wise man (*paṇḍitapurisa*) who rebuked a destructive monkey (*vānara*), the past counterpart of the leaf-basket destroyer [Fausböll 1879].
